title: Review of c33's phoretic Janus composites: fresh seed 7 reproduces capped A bodies that travel 6.7 body lengths, against 2.1 in the reciprocal twin (Supported)
summary: Labkit re-run of world.py on seed 7 (rerun/seed7) and the matched reciprocal twin (WORLD_P mu=[[1,1],[1,0.5]], i.e. mu_A2=+1, same seed, recip/seed7), 400 frames, t=200. From the uniform random gas (particles.png t=0), A clusters with B caps on one side form by t~35-50 and persist (tracks.png #35: a compact composite with its cap held from t=23 to t=200). World: 44 long-lived tracks move >= 1 body length, max 6.7 body lengths, max speed 0.37; reciprocal twin: 13 tracks, max 2.1 body lengths, max speed 0.20, with round mixed clusters. Composites also merge and grow (max/min area of persistent tracks 7.25), so individuality holds between merger events.

observations.S: rerun/seed7/particles.png t=0: uniform random gas; composites by t~35-50
observations.I: rerun/seed7/tracks.png #35: one capped composite tracked t=23-200; 7 persistent tracks
observations.M: rerun/seed7/FACTS.md: 44 tracks move >= 1 body length, max 6.7, against recip/seed7/FACTS.md: 13 tracks, max 2.1

seeds_run.result: pass: max 6.7 body lengths vs 2.1 in the reciprocal twin

controls_run.M: recip/seed7: reciprocal twin (mu_A2=+1), same seed, grid and duration

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed, labkit field tracking only: 'body length' uses the field blob, and composites merge and grow over the run, so the longest runs may span merger events. The motility is the known non-reciprocal phoretic mechanism (Soto & Golestanian 2014), as the claim says.
